headline: South Asia: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources.
- Western Russia: Russian strikes on warehouses in Odesa Oblast cause major fires, killing 1 and injuring 2 – photos.
- Asia: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings, 9 acquitted.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Escalating domestic violence impacting St James churches.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: Escalating domestic violence impacting St James churches.
WESTERN BUREAU: Domestic violence is emerging as an increasingly common issue confronting churches across St James, as pastors are routinely called upon to counsel people struggling with troubled relationships and family conflicts. The Reverend Godfrey Francis, secretary of the St James Ministers Fraternal, said the pressures of modern life, coupled with poor communication and weak conflict resolution skills, were helping to fuel the problem, leaving churches to confront the fallout.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: ‘I used to say, ‘Good job, police’, but now I feel it’.
Relatives of 35-year-old businessman Jordon Perry Smith took their grief and anger to the streets of Seaford Town, Westmoreland, on Monday, demanding answers over his fatal shooting during a police operation. The protest came three days after Smith was killed at his home in an incident police sources have described as a shoot-out, while his relatives continue to reject that account and accuse members of the Constabulary Force of executing him.

The U.S. Army awarded Lockheed Martin a PrSM contract worth up to $1.2 billion.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources.
Security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram from Afghanistan and also effectively responded to firing by the Afghan Taliban, security sources said on Tuesday. According to the sources, the terrorists tried to infiltrate the border from Nangarhar and Paktia in Afghanistan. They identified the terrorists as those belonging to Fitna-al-Khawarij — a term that the state uses for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: CDF Munir says armed forces remain resolute in defeating terrorism, ensuring lasting peace: ISPR.
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir said on Tuesday that the armed forces remained resolute in defeating terrorism and ensuring lasting peace and stability, according to the military’s media wing. Field Marshal Munir made the statement while visiting Peshawar Corps Headquarters, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. He was received by the Peshawar Corps commander.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: 'Terrific man' Shehbaz gets special mention during Trump's UNGA speech.
United States President Donald Trump on Tuesday called Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif a “terrific man” during his address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) as he once again mentioned his role in ending the Pakistan-India conflict in May 2025. During a speech that covered the conflict in Iran, artificial intelligence and criticism of the UN, Trump once again listed conflicts that he had played a role in ending. “Since I took office, it has been my honour to help settle eight wars, and in so doing, become friendly with the leaders of many of those countries,” Trump said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Pakistan, 7 other Muslim nations call upon Israel to fulfil its commitment under Gaza plan.
Pakistan joined other Muslim countries on Tuesday in calling for Israel to “immediately fulfill its outstanding commitments” under the first phase of a plan aimed at ending the conflict in Gaza. The demand was made in a joint statement attributed to the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates after they met on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Sri Lanka’s High Court has found 15 of the 24 men accused of being directly involved in the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings guilty. The attacks killed 279 people and wounded around 500. The three-judge bench found that 14 of the accused were guilty on all charges, which included murder, conspiracy to commit terrorism and possessing firearms and explosives under the Prevention of Terrorism Act. The drill matters not only because it highlights the growing integration between the agency and Taiwan’s navy, experts argue, but also because missile-armed coastguard vessels would add another threat the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) would have to account for in a conflict.
